title: Patch: a daily move is answered before its email and pushes go out, so a slow mail or push service never holds the player's move
thread:
**Issue #3856 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #3856: Patch: a daily move is answered before its email and pushes go out, so a slow mail or push service never holds the player's move
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In a daily game, the move that hands the game to the other player also sends them an email and a phone or browser notification. Today the server waits for those to go out before it tells the mover that their move went through. Normally that adds a moment.

When the mail service or a push service is slow or down, each send waits up to ten seconds, one device after another. A send that fails is never marked as sent, so while the outage lasts, the same wait comes back on every action the other player takes during their own turn: a whole turn of ten-second clicks, or a timeout error for a move that was in fact saved.

Once built, the server answers the move first and sends the notifications just after. A player never waits on them, and nothing goes unsent: the hourly sweep still sends whatever failed.

## Why

- **Where it waits.** `act` (`crates/server/src/daily/games.rs:626-628`) awaits `crate::daily::notify::after_move` before it answers. So do an accept (`daily/invites.rs:280`) and a seek that pairs at once (`daily/invites.rs:365`).
- **How long.** `after_move` (`daily/notify.rs:258`) runs `notify_one` for both players in turn. `notify_one` sends the email first, with a 10 s timeout (`PLAYER_EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `crates/server/src/config.rs:1594`). Then `send_pushes` posts to each device in turn, 10 s each (`PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS`) for up to 10 devices (`PUSH_MAX_DEVICES`, `config.rs:1599-1606`).
- **Why it repeats.**
  - A failed email or push sets neither `last_email_at` nor `last_push_at`, so `decide_notify` (`crates/shared/src/notify.rs`) finds the channel due again at the next action.
  - The player holding the move has their own game waiting on them, so each of their actions re-sends inline.
  - At worst, one action waits 2 × (10 s + 10 × 10 s). That is past the client's 75 s request timeout (`API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), so the player sees an error for a move the server stored.
- **The pattern exists.**
  - Alerts are queued to a task (`crates/server/src/alerts.rs:252`), and a bug report's filing is spawned (`crates/server/src/bug_reports.rs:437`).
  - The sweep, every `DAILY_SWEEP_MINUTES` (`daily/notify.rs:279`, `:355`), already re-sends whatever is still due.
  - §9.13 asks only that the server decide after each move, for both players, and at each sweep. Nothing there needs the answer to wait.

## Proposal

- **A notifier task.** Hand the post-move notification to one background task fed by a bounded channel, as `alerts.rs` queues its sends, instead of awaiting it at the three call sites. The task takes profiles in order and skips one already queued, so two quick moves don't race into two pushes. The queue's size is a named constant in `crates/server/src/config.rs` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
- **Nothing is lost.** A profile dropped from a full queue, or one the server stopped while sending, is sent by the next sweep, since an unfinished send is never marked.
- **What stays.** `push_social` (the badge update) stays as it is.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/daily/games.rs`, `daily/invites.rs`, `daily/notify.rs`
- `crates/server/src/config.rs`
- `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`
- SPEC §9.13 (Notifications): one line saying the decision runs after the answer and never holds it

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A server test with a mail service that holds its answer (a variant of `fake_service`, `tests/api/daily.rs:230`): ending a turn answers well before the hold ends, and the email still arrives. Fails today.
- [ ] A server test: with the push service failing, two actions in a row by the player holding the move each answer at once.
- [ ] A server test: a profile queued twice before the task reaches it is notified once.
- [ ] The existing daily tests that read the email after a move wait for it instead of assuming it went first.
- [ ] Green: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Size and risks

Small to medium, about 5 files.

- **Tests.** Tests that expect the mail to have gone by the time the move answers must wait for the task.
- **Delay.** A slow send now delays only other notifications, and the sweep backs those up.
- **Conflicts.** #3844 (a 403 deletes a subscription) also changes `send_pushes`, so whichever lands second merges around the other.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

<!-- jackioh-bot -->

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43503972914)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

A daily move's answer no longer waits for its email and push. `daily::notify::after_move` queues both players for one background notifier task and returns at once. The task decides for each queued profile in order and skips a profile that is already waiting in the queue. A full queue drops the profile, and the next sweep sends whatever is still due. This covers all three call sites: `act`, `accept` and a seek that pairs at once. Also covered:
- the queue size is a named constant (CLAUDE.md rule 9);
- `push_social` stays as it is;
- SPEC §9.13 gets one sentence;
- the three server tests from the issue are added;
- the existing tests that assumed the notification had gone by the time the move answered now wait for the task.

## Files to touch

| File | | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/config.rs` | change | New `DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE`, beside `PLAYER_EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MS` (about line 1594). |
| `crates/server/src/daily/notify.rs` | change | New `NotifyQueue` and `start`. `after_move` becomes a sync fn with no `now`. Header docs get a bullet. |
| `crates/server/src/daily/mod.rs` | change | `DailyState` gets `pub notifier: notify::NotifyQueue`, built in `new`. |
| `crates/server/src/daily/games.rs` | change | `act`, line 645: the call loses `.await` and `now`. |
| `crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs` | change | `accept` (line 280) and `seek` (line 365): same edit. |
| `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` | change | New helpers and 3 new tests; the 2 push tests wait for the task. |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | §9.13 "Notifications": one sentence in the last sub-bullet. |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | One sentence in the "Telling a player" paragraph (about line 787). |

**Do not touch:**
- `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`;
- `crates/shared` (`decide_notify` stays pure and unchanged);
- the engine, cards and AI crates;
- `apps/web`, including the generated `wire/`: `serverConfig.ts` is written from an explicit list in `tests/export_config.rs`, so the new constant changes nothing there;
- `crates/server/tests/support/test_app.rs`: `DailyState::new(mailer, push)` keeps its signature;
- `send_push` and `send_pushes` internals (#3844 edits them);
- `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/rulings/`, `spec/pending/`.

Governing text: SPEC §9.13 (Notifications), CLAUDE.md rule 9 (named constants) and rule 4 (the server crate may use tokio). This is operational, not a rules decision, so it needs **no ruling note** and no `spec/pending` file.

## Steps

1. **`config.rs`.** Add, after `PLAYER_EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MS`:
   ```rust
   /// §9.13: how many profiles wait for the notifier's task (`daily::notify::NotifyQueue`) before a new
   /// one is dropped; the next sweep decides for it, since nothing unsent is ever marked sent.
   pub const DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE: usize = 256;
   ```

2. **`daily/notify.rs`, imports.**
   - Change `use std::sync::Arc;` to `use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};`.
   - Add `use tokio::sync::{mpsc, watch};`.
   - Add `lock` to the `crate::api::http::{…}` import list (it is `pub(crate)`).
   - Add `DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE` to the `crate::config::{…}` list.

3. **`daily/notify.rs`, the queue.** Put this above `after_move`:
   ```rust
   /// The profiles the notifier's task has yet to decide for (§9.13). One task, started by the first move,
   /// takes them in the order they came; a move never waits for it.
   pub struct NotifyQueue {
       /// The task's channel, `DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE` deep, made together with the task.
       sender: OnceLock<mpsc::Sender<String>>,
       /// The profiles in the channel. One in it is not queued again, so two moves before the task
       /// reaches a profile decide for it once; the task takes it out as it takes it off the channel.
       queued: Mutex<IndexSet<String>>,
       /// Profiles queued or being decided for; `idle` waits for it to reach 0.
       busy: watch::Sender<usize>,
   }
   impl Default for NotifyQueue {
       fn default() -> NotifyQueue {
           NotifyQueue { sender: OnceLock::new(), queued: Mutex::new(IndexSet::new()), busy: watch::Sender::new(0) }
       }
   }
   ```
   `Default` is needed because clippy's `new_without_default` is denied.

   Add `impl NotifyQueue` with two methods.

   - `fn enqueue(&self, app: &Arc<App>, profiles: &[&str])`:
     - `let sender = self.sender.get_or_init(|| start(app));`
     - `let mut queued = lock(&self.queued);`
     - For each `profile_id`: `continue` if `queued.contains(*profile_id)`.
     - Otherwise `match sender.try_send((*profile_id).to_string())`:
       - on `Ok(())`: `queued.insert(..)` and `self.busy.send_modify(|busy| *busy += 1)`;
       - on `Err(error)` (full or closed): `log_warn("daily.notify.dropped", json!({ "profileId": profile_id, "message": error.to_string() }))`.
     - Hold the lock across `try_send` (it never awaits). That keeps the set and the channel consistent: the task's removal waits for the insert.
   - `pub async fn idle(&self)`: `let mut busy = self.busy.subscribe(); let _ = busy.wait_for(|busy| *busy == 0).await;`. Copy the shape of `practice::all_settled`. Doc: "Resolves once nothing is queued or being decided for. Tests wait on it; the server never does: what a stop leaves unsent the next sweep sends."

4. **`daily/notify.rs`, the task.** Add this beside the queue:
   ```rust
   fn start(app: &Arc<App>) -> mpsc::Sender<String> {
       let (sender, mut receiver) = mpsc::channel(DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE);
       let app = Arc::downgrade(app);
       tokio::spawn(async move {
           while let Some(profile_id) = receiver.recv().await {
               let Some(app) = app.upgrade() else { break };
               // Taken off: a move that lands while it is decided for queues it again.
               lock(&app.daily.notifier.queued).shift_remove(profile_id.as_str());
               if let Err(error) = notify_one(&app, &profile_id, app.daily.now()).await {
                   log_warn("daily.notify_failed", json!({ "profileId": profile_id, "message": error.message }));
               }
               app.daily.notifier.busy.send_modify(|busy| *busy = busy.saturating_sub(1));
           }
       });
       sender
   }
   ```
   The task holds only a `Weak<App>`, so the `Sender` inside `DailyState` drops with the app. `recv` then returns `None` and the task ends; there is no cycle. Pattern: `alerts::Notifier::start`.

5. **`daily/notify.rs`, `after_move`.** Replace the existing fn with:
   ```rust
   /// After a move or a start: queues both players for the notifier's task and returns, so the answer
   /// never waits on a mail or push service (§9.13). A profile the queue cannot take is decided for by
   /// the next sweep.
   pub(crate) fn after_move(app: &Arc<App>, profiles: &[&str]) {
       app.daily.notifier.enqueue(app, profiles);
   }
   ```
   - `notify_one` and the sweep stay as they are.
   - Add a bullet to the file header: "After a move the decision runs on one task (`NotifyQueue`), after the answer."

6. **`daily/mod.rs`.**
   - Add to `DailyState`: `/// §9.13: the moves' notifications waiting for their task (`notify::after_move`).` and `pub notifier: notify::NotifyQueue,`.
   - In `DailyState::new`, add `notifier: notify::NotifyQueue::default(),` to the struct literal.
   - Update the `[`notify`]` line in the module doc to "…the sweep, the settings and the task that sends after a move".

7. **Call sites.**
   - `games.rs:645`: `crate::daily::notify::after_move(app, &[&a, &b]);`.
   - `invites.rs:280`: `crate::daily::notify::after_move(app, &[&me, &invite.from_profile]);`.
   - `invites.rs:365`: `crate::daily::notify::after_move(app, &[&me, &other.from_profile]);`.
   - `now` is still used elsewhere in each fn, so no unused-variable warning.

8. **Spec.** In `spec/09-architecture.md`, the bullet "The server decides after each move, for both players, and at each sweep. A channel whose keys the server was not given is off." gets this sentence inserted before "A channel whose keys…": "The decision after a move runs once the move has been answered and never holds it: a slow or failing mail or push service delays only the notifications queued behind it, and a profile the server did not reach is decided for at the next sweep."

9. **README.** In `crates/server/README.md`, "Telling a player", after "each move decides for both players", add: "A move is answered first: `daily::notify::after_move` queues both players for one task (`NotifyQueue`, `DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE` deep, a profile already waiting is not queued twice) that decides for each in turn; a profile the full queue refused, or the server dropped at a stop, is decided for by the next sweep (#3856)."

10. **Tests** (below): add the helpers first, then the three tests, then the two edits to existing tests.

## Tests

All are in `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`. Add `use std::time::Duration;` and `use tokio::sync::Semaphore;`. Change the store import to `jackioh_server::db::store::{DailyNotifyRow, MatchStatus, PushSubRow}`.

**Helpers** (module level, near `fake_service`):
- `held_service(status: StatusCode) -> (String, Arc<StdMutex<Vec<(String, HeaderMap, Vec<u8>)>>>, Arc<Semaphore>)`.
  - Copy `fake_service`'s router, listener and `take` handler.
  - The state is `(seen, status, gate)` with `gate = Arc::new(Semaphore::new(0))`.
  - The handler records the request first, then does `let _held = gate.acquire().await;`, then returns `status` for every path.
  - `gate.add_permits(1)` opens it for good, because each request returns the permit on drop.
  - Leave `fake_service` unchanged.
- `const ANSWERS_WITHIN: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);` with a comment: under the 10 s a send waits (`PLAYER_EMAIL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS`), so a move that waited on a send fails it.
- `async fn answers_at_once<T>(what: &str, future: impl std::future::Future<Output = T>) -> T`: `tokio::time::timeout(ANSWERS_WITHIN, future).await.unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!("{what} waited on the held service"))`.
- `async fn eventually(what: &str, mut done: impl FnMut() -> bool)`: polls every 10 ms up to 10 s, then panics `"never: {what}"`.
- `async fn notifier_idle(app: &Arc<App>)`: `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(20), app.daily.notifier.idle()).await.expect("the notifier goes idle")`.
- `async fn subscribe(app: &Arc<App>, who: &Account, n: i64, endpoint: String)`: adds a `PushSubRow` with `browser_keys()`, copying the inline block of `a_push_subscription_answered_410_is_deleted`.
- `async fn notify_row(app: &Arc<App>, who: &Account) -> DailyNotifyRow`: `tx.daily_notify_get(&who.id)`.

**New tests:**

1. `a_move_is_answered_before_its_email_goes_and_the_email_still_arrives`
   - Build the app with `mail_api: Some(format!("{mail_api}/emails"))` from `held_service(StatusCode::OK)`, plus Ada and Bo as friends.
   - `daily_game(&app, &ada, &bo, 1)` is wrapped in `answers_at_once`.
   - `eventually` the service has seen 1 request.
   - `answers_at_once` over `past_the_mulligan(..)` followed by `one_move(&app, [&ada, &bo], &match_id, 1)` (the holder ends the turn).
   - Assert `seen.len() == 1`: one mail is held, and the task is serial.
   - Then `gate.add_permits(1)` and `notifier_idle`.
   - Assert the recorded mails went to exactly `{ada.id}@example.test` and `{bo.id}@example.test`, one each (the 6 h gap holds back any repeat), and `last_email_at.is_some()` for both via `notify_row`.
   - Fails today: the first `daily_game` waits the mail's 10 s timeout, past 5 s.

2. `a_failing_push_service_never_holds_the_actions_of_the_player_it_waits_on`
   - Use `held_service(StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR)` and `push_keys: Some(vapid_pair())`.
   - Subscribe Ada at `{push_api}/push/1/ada`.
   - Start three games with `daily_game(&app, &bo, &ada, d)` for `d` in 1, 3 and 7, each in `answers_at_once`. The first one's push goes out and is held, so `eventually` the service has seen a request.
   - Game 1 stays waiting on Ada, so her push stays due on every later action. This is what made each of her actions re-send inline.
   - Then `answers_at_once("Ada's first action", one_move(&app, [&ada, &bo], &g2, 1))` and the same for `g3` with nonce 2.
   - Then `gate.add_permits(1)`, `notifier_idle`, and assert `notify_row(&app, &ada).await.last_push_at == None`: a failed push is never marked, so the sweep sends it.

3. `a_profile_queued_twice_before_the_task_reaches_it_is_notified_once`
   - Same held push service (500) and Ada subscribed, with `g1 = daily_game(&app, &bo, &ada, 1)`.
   - The accept queues `[ada, bo]`. The task takes Ada and her push is held; wait with `eventually` for `seen.len() == 1`. Bo stays queued.
   - Bo moves in `g1` with `one_move(&app, [&bo, &ada], &g1, 1)`: this queues Ada once, because Bo is already queued.
   - Start `g2 = daily_game(&app, &bo, &ada, 3)` and `one_move(&app, [&bo, &ada], &g2, 2)`: both players are already queued, so these skip.
   - Then `gate.add_permits(1)` and `notifier_idle`.
   - Assert `seen.len() == 2`: the held send plus one queued decision. Without the dedupe it is 4. Ada keeps games waiting (her mulligans), so the second decision does send.

**Edits to existing tests:**
- `a_push_subscription_answered_410_is_deleted`: add `notifier_idle(&app).await;` right after `daily_game(&app, &bo, &ada, 1).await;`, before `seen` is read.
- `a_push_follows_no_redirect`: same line after its `daily_game`, before the `hops` assertion.
- Tests that start games on an app with no channels need no change; their task is a no-op.

**Commands:**
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily`
- `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo jackioh spec check`
- `cargo jackioh patches check`
- Before the final run, confirm the 3 new tests fail on the base by stashing nothing: write the tests first and run them once before steps 2–7.

## Done when

- [ ] `after_move` is sync, takes no `now`, and none of `act`, `accept` or `seek` awaits a send.
- [ ] `NotifyQueue` is bounded by `DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE`, which is a named constant.
- [ ] Profiles are decided in order and a queued profile is not queued twice.
- [ ] A full or closed queue logs `daily.notify.dropped`, and the sweep covers it.
- [ ] The three issue tests pass, and failed before the change.
- [ ] The two existing push tests wait with `notifier_idle`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily` is green.
- [ ] The clippy, fmt, spec and patches checks above are green.
- [ ] The §9.13 sentence and the README sentence are in.
- [ ] `git status` shows no change under `apps/web/src/wire`.

## Risks

- **Test timing.** The test runtime is current-thread, so the task runs only when a test awaits something that suspends (`eventually`, `notifier_idle`). `notifier_idle` starts after `busy` is at least 1, because the enqueue is synchronous in the handler, so it cannot return early.
- **Failed push retries.** A failed push still re-sends on every later decision. That is unchanged, and now it only delays other notifications behind it.
- **Sweep versus the task.** A sweep that decides for a profile while the task is mid-send for it can send twice. The same overlap existed before (inline send versus sweep); `begin_sweep` guards sweep against sweep only. Left alone.
- **Shutdown.** The task is not in `spawn_loops`, so `stop_loops` does not abort it. The process ending kills it. `notify_one` commits before it sends, so no store connection is held during a slow send and `pg::close` is not delayed. An unmarked send repeats at the next sweep. A narrow window remains where a send went out but its mark was not written, which would repeat one email or push.
- **Task death.** If the task panicked, later moves would only log `dropped`, and the sweep keeps notifying. `notify_one` returns `Result`, so a panic is not expected.
- **#3844 conflict.** #3844 edits `send_pushes`, which this plan does not touch.
- **Determinism and hidden information.** None of the pure crates is touched. The client contract is unchanged: the move's response body is the same, it just arrives sooner.

## Decisions the task did not settle

- **Task start.** The task starts lazily at the first move, holding a `Weak<App>`.
  - Rejected: a `spawn_supervised` loop in `app.rs`. It needs the receiver handed through `App` and the test app starting it, and it breaks `DailyState::new`'s signature.
- **Dedupe.**
  - A profile leaves the set when the task takes it, so a move landing mid-decision queues it again. Its state changed, so a fresh decision is needed.
  - Rejected: dedupe only against waiting items and in-flight ones.
- **Clock.** `now` is read by the task (`app.daily.now()`) when it reaches the profile, not carried from the move. A deduped item has no single move time, and marking `last_*_at` with a stale time would lie.
- **`idle()`.** A small public seam, used only by tests, instead of polling the fake store. It makes the "exactly N requests" assertions deterministic.
- **Queue size.** 256, not 64 (`ALERT_QUEUE`'s value): one slow send can take up to 110 s, so a burst of moves needs headroom before the sweep has to catch up.

## Open questions

- The maintainer's second comment is cut off: "But then you should clean up the notif…". This plan reads it as tidying the notification code it touches (docs and comments in `notify.rs`, the README and the spec), and nothing wider. If it meant something else, such as removing the failed-send retry on every action, a person must say so. It is not required to build this issue.
````

## Risks

- **Test timing.** The test runtime is current-thread, so the task runs only when a test awaits something that suspends (`eventually`, `notifier_idle`). `notifier_idle` starts after `busy` is at least 1, because the enqueue is synchronous in the handler, so it cannot return early.
- **Failed push retries.** A failed push still re-sends on every later decision. That is unchanged, and now it only delays other notifications behind it.
- **Sweep versus the task.** A sweep that decides for a profile while the task is mid-send for it can send twice. The same overlap existed before (inline send versus sweep); `begin_sweep` guards sweep against sweep only. Left alone.
- **Shutdown.** The task is not in `spawn_loops`, so `stop_loops` does not abort it. The process ending kills it. `notify_one` commits before it sends, so no store connection is held during a slow send and `pg::close` is not delayed. An unmarked send repeats at the next sweep. A narrow window remains where a send went out but its mark was not written, which would repeat one email or push.
- **Task death.** If the task panicked, later moves would only log `dropped`, and the sweep keeps notifying. `notify_one` returns `Result`, so a panic is not expected.
- **#3844 conflict.** #3844 edits `send_pushes`, which this plan does not touch.
- **Determinism and hidden information.** None of the pure crates is touched. The client contract is unchanged: the move's response body is the same, it just arrives sooner.

## Decisions the task did not settle

- **Task start.** The task starts lazily at the first move, holding a `Weak<App>`.
  - Rejected: a `spawn_supervised` loop in `app.rs`. It needs the receiver handed through `App` and the test app starting it, and it breaks `DailyState::new`'s signature.
- **Dedupe.**
  - A profile leaves the set when the task takes it, so a move landing mid-decision queues it again. Its state changed, so a fresh decision is needed.
  - Rejected: dedupe only against waiting items and in-flight ones.
- **Clock.** `now` is read by the task (`app.daily.now()`) when it reaches the profile, not carried from the move. A deduped item has no single move time, and marking `last_*_at` with a stale time would lie.
- **`idle()`.** A small public seam, used only by tests, instead of polling the fake store. It makes the "exactly N requests" assertions deterministic.
- **Queue size.** 256, not 64 (`ALERT_QUEUE`'s value): one slow send can take up to 110 s, so a burst of moves needs headroom before the sweep has to catch up.

## Done when

- [ ] `after_move` is sync, takes no `now`, and none of `act`, `accept` or `seek` awaits a send.
- [ ] `NotifyQueue` is bounded by `DAILY_NOTIFY_QUEUE`, which is a named constant.
- [ ] Profiles are decided in order and a queued profile is not queued twice.
- [ ] A full or closed queue logs `daily.notify.dropped`, and the sweep covers it.
- [ ] The three issue tests pass, and failed before the change.
- [ ] The two existing push tests wait with `notifier_idle`.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily` is green.
- [ ] The clippy, fmt, spec and patches checks above are green.
- [ ] The §9.13 sentence and the README sentence are in.
- [ ] `git status` shows no change under `apps/web/src/wire`.

## Risks

- **Test timing.** The test runtime is current-thread, so the task runs only when a test awaits something that suspends (`eventually`, `notifier_idle`). `notifier_idle` starts after `busy` is at least 1, because the enqueue is synchronous in the handler, so it cannot return early.
- **Failed push retries.** A failed push still re-sends on every later decision. That is unchanged, and now it only delays other notifications behind it.
- **Sweep versus the task.** A sweep that decides for a profile while the task is mid-send for it can send twice. The same overlap existed before (inline send versus sweep); `begin_sweep` guards sweep against sweep only. Left alone.
- **Shutdown.** The task is not in `spawn_loops`, so `stop_loops` does not abort it. The process ending kills it. `notify_one` commits before it sends, so no store connection is held during a slow send and `pg::close` is not delayed. An unmarked send repeats at the next sweep. A narrow window remains where a send went out but its mark was not written, which would repeat one email or push.
- **Task death.** If the task panicked, later moves would only log `dropped`, and the sweep keeps notifying. `notify_one` returns `Result`, so a panic is not expected.
- **#3844 conflict.** #3844 edits `send_pushes`, which this plan does not touch.
- **Determinism and hidden information.** None of the pure crates is touched. The client contract is unchanged: the move's response body is the same, it just arrives sooner.

## Decisions the task did not settle

- **Task start.** The task starts lazily at the first move, holding a `Weak<App>`.
  - Rejected: a `spawn_supervised` loop in `app.rs`. It needs the receiver handed through `App` and the test app starting it, and it breaks `DailyState::new`'s signature.
- **Dedupe.**
  - A profile leaves the set when the task takes it, so a move landing mid-decision queues it again. Its state changed, so a fresh decision is needed.
  - Rejected: dedupe only against waiting items and in-flight ones.
- **Clock.** `now` is read by the task (`app.daily.now()`) when it reaches the profile, not carried from the move. A deduped item has no single move time, and marking `last_*_at` with a stale time would lie.
- **`idle()`.** A small public seam, used only by tests, instead of polling the fake store. It makes the "exactly N requests" assertions deterministic.
- **Queue size.** 256, not 64 (`ALERT_QUEUE`'s value): one slow send can take up to 110 s, so a burst of moves needs headroom before the sweep has to catch up.

This plan reads it as tidying the notification code it touches (docs and comments in `notify.rs`, the README and the spec), and nothing wider. If it meant something else, such as removing the failed-send retry on every action, a person must say so. It is not required to build this issue.
